text:
Ottawa arrives off a 6-5 overtime loss at LAK, where Quinton Byfield won it, and it's 2-2-1 in its last five without William Eklund, Hayden Hodgson and Warren Foegele. San Jose beat VAN 3-2 after trailing by two, missing Alexander Wennberg and Igor Chernyshov, with Collin Graf stepping onto the Celebrini and Smith line. These teams met Oct. 22, and the Sharks won 6-2, a game our numbers say they deserved to win only 28% of the time, meaning the score flattered them.

That's the story again here. OTT has taken 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five to SJS's 44%, and the Sharks give up the most per 60 minutes. Their results lean on Yaroslav Askarov (projected), who is at +7.7 goals saved above expected this season, though he was -19.4 last year. Samuel Ersson (projected) is at -3.2 now and -17.8 last season. Ottawa's power play, at 0.80 expected goals a game, meets a penalty kill allowing 0.90, and the Senators take five penalties a game.

For Ottawa, we like Tim Stützle at 38% to score and Drake Batherson at 36%, riding a six-game point streak. Mason Marchment is one goal from 100 career goals. Macklin Celebrini leads San Jose at 43%. Our under-the-radar picks are Stephen Halliday, whose third-line shots have been dangerous (15% to score), and Shane Pinto, 57% for a point, with Pinto picking up Eklund's minutes.
